title: Assessing Iowa’s Solar Power Capacity Under Current and Projected Climate Conditions
content: This study examines the trends in solar energy potential in Iowa between two 25-year time periods using solar insolation data. The purpose of this study is to quantify the amount of energy that could be generated by solar panels in Iowa, and furthermore, quantify the amount of carbon dioxide emissions that could be reduced by converting a portion of Iowa’s farmland into solar panel farms. Lastly, this study discusses the practicality of converting enough farmland into solar panel farms in order to generate a substantial amount of energy. We obtained past and future scenario solar insolation data from the RegCM4 and calculated the monthly solar energy potential and the possible carbon dioxide emissions reductions in Iowa and Oregon for both time periods. Upon completion of the study, we found that the average monthly carbon dioxide emissions in both Iowa and Oregon are very similar between the past and future scenarios. Additionally, our results suggest that the change in solar energy potential between months is more substantial than the change in solar energy potential between years. Finally, we found that the amount of land that would need to be converted to solar panel farms in order to generate a substantial amount of energy is a very reasonable portion of farmland. Our results imply that the amount of solar energy that will be available in the future will be similar to the amount of solar energy that is available today, and only a small percentage of Iowa’s farmland would need to be converted to solar panel farms to substantially reduce monthly carbon dioxide emissions.
